activities.title: Box Breathing
activities.description: Breathe in four equal steps to steady yourself before a quiz or presentation.
steps: Sit upright with both feet on the floor.
Use the timer at the top of this page.
Breathe in for 4, hold for 4, out for 4, hold for 4.
Repeat for six rounds.

activities.title: 4-7-8 Breathing
activities.description: A longer out-breath that helps a busy mind slow down.
steps: Rest the tip of your tongue behind your top teeth.
Breathe in through your nose for 4.
Hold gently for 7.
Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 8.
Do four rounds, then breathe normally.

activities.title: Slow Calm Breathing
activities.description: In for 4, out for 6. Easy enough to do in bed or between classes.
steps: Get comfortable, sitting or lying down.
Breathe in through your nose for 4.
Breathe out softly for 6.
Continue for eight rounds.

activities.title: Study-Break Desk Stretch
activities.description: Loosen your neck, shoulders and back after long hours at a laptop.
steps: Roll your shoulders back slowly five times.
Tilt your head to each side and hold for 15 seconds.
Interlace your fingers and stretch your arms overhead.
Twist gently to each side in your chair.
Stand up and shake out your hands.

activities.title: Pomodoro Reset
activities.description: Study for 25 minutes, then take a real 5-minute break away from screens.
steps: Choose one task only.
Set a 25-minute timer and silence your phone.
When it ends, stand up and look out of a window.
Drink some water before the next round.

activities.title: Five-Minute Walk
activities.description: A short walk around campus to restart your energy.
steps: Leave your phone in your pocket.
Walk at a comfortable pace for five minutes.
Notice three things you have not noticed before.
Come back and start with the easiest task.

activities.title: One Small Task
activities.description: Pick a task so small it feels easy, and finish just that.
steps: Write down the assignment you are avoiding.
Break off a piece that takes ten minutes.
Do only that piece.
Tick it off and notice how it feels.

activities.title: Gentle Morning Stretch
activities.description: Wake your body up slowly before the university day.
steps: Stretch your arms overhead while still lying down.
Hug your knees to your chest for 20 seconds.
Sit up and roll your neck slowly.
Stand and reach for your toes, bending your knees if needed.

activities.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
activities.description: Bring your attention back to the room using your five senses.
steps: Name 5 things you can see.
Name 4 things you can touch.
Name 3 things you can hear.
Name 2 things you can smell.
Name 1 thing you can taste.

activities.title: Write It Down
activities.description: Move looping thoughts from your head onto paper.
steps: Write every worry on paper for five minutes, without stopping.
Circle the ones you can act on this week.
Write one small action next to each circled worry.
Close the notebook.

activities.title: Send One Message
activities.description: Reconnect with someone using one simple message.
steps: Think of a classmate, cousin or old friend.
Send a short message, such as asking how their week is going.
You do not need a long conversation; a hello is enough.

activities.title: Campus Connection Ideas
activities.description: Small ways to meet people who share your interests.
steps: Look at your university's societies or clubs list.
Choose one event this week that sounds interesting.
Sit next to someone new in one class.
Ask a classmate to study together in the library.

activities.title: Gratitude Note
activities.description: Write down three good things from today, however small.
steps: Find a quiet moment at the end of the day.
Write three things that went well.
For one of them, write who was part of it.
Consider thanking that person.

activities.title: My Trusted-Person Plan
activities.description: Decide in advance who you could talk to when things feel heavy.
steps: List two or three people you trust: family, friends or teachers.
Next to each, write how you would reach them.
Write one sentence you could use to start, such as asking if they have time to talk.
Add your university counselling office to the list.

activities.title: Get Help Contacts
activities.description: Pakistan helplines and emergency numbers, all in one place.
steps: Open the Get Help page.
Save one helpline number in your phone.
If you are in danger right now, call 1122.

activities.title: Body-Scan Relaxation
activities.description: Relax each part of your body from head to toe before sleep.
steps: Lie down and close your eyes.
Notice your forehead and let it soften.
Move slowly down: jaw, shoulders, arms, chest, stomach, legs, feet.
If your mind wanders, gently return to the last body part.

activities.title: Sleep-Friendly Habits
activities.description: Simple habits that make falling asleep easier.
steps: Try to sleep and wake at similar times each day.
Put your phone away 30 minutes before bed.
Avoid tea, coffee and energy drinks late in the evening.
Keep your room dark and cool.

activities.title: Child's Pose and Gentle Yoga
activities.description: Slow, restful positions for days when you feel drained.
steps: Kneel on a mat or carpet and sit back on your heels.
Fold forward and rest your forehead down, arms in front.
Stay for ten slow breaths.
Roll onto your back and hug your knees.
Move gently and skip any position that hurts.

activities.title: Permission to Rest
activities.description: Ten minutes of rest without guilt and without a screen.
steps: Set a 10-minute timer.
Lie down or sit somewhere comfortable.
Do nothing productive on purpose.
When the timer ends, drink some water.

activities.title: Calming Nature Video
activities.description: Watch a quiet nature clip and breathe along with it.
steps: Turn the volume low.
Watch the video and slow your breathing.
Notice how your shoulders feel at the end.
